svg.aria-label: Fig 6. Planned review console and audit trail. Two queue trays hold AI-flagged claims and a random QA sample. A console screen shows the timeline of synthetic claim SYN-C-000042: the LLM triage, the CCI gate sending it to a human, the reviewer sending it to the writer, the appeal draft with four of four statements cited, and an approval that waits for the reviewer. An append-only audit trail of linked blocks stores the hash of each previous block. An approvals panel has approve, edit and reject buttons. A blue dotted track takes a reviewer edit to the feedback station, where it becomes an eval case. Planned, not built.

svg.text: Synthetic claims only. Planned design, not built.
every AI action writes an audit_event
1 Two queues: claims the AI flags (wide set, guardrail hit, high dollar) and a random QA
sample of claims that the AI handled alone. The random sample measures true quality.
2 The claim timeline shows each AI and human action, the model, the prompt version and the sources.
3 The audit trail is append-only. Each row stores the hash of the row before it.
4 External or money actions (send an appeal, place a call) wait for a human click.
Write-offs and refunds need two people.
5 A reviewer edit, with a reason, becomes an eval case. The gate is then recalibrated.
Tracks. Chevrons show the direction. black: work moves on. blue dotted: feedback.
Short links between audit blocks: each block stores the hash of the block before it.
HUMAN CLICK FOR SEND OR CALL
